The fields a dictionary makes read-only on every row

dictionary_readonly.Rd

The fields whose annotation carries @READONLY outside any @IF(...). A tag inside an @IF holds only on the rows its condition picks, and the field can be written on the others: server and project_id are locked that way once a row carries a seal (decided on 2026-11-09), and they are intent fields, not fields of the channel. Counted with the rest, they would read as read-only fields the live register lost, on a register that has not imported the tag yet, and the round would stop.

Usage

dictionary_readonly(dictionary)

Arguments

dictionary

A data dictionary, with Variable / Field Name and Field Annotation.

Value

The names of those fields, in dictionary order.

Details

The @IF is cut with its parentheses balanced, skipping what stands inside quotes, since a condition can hold a parenthesis of its own; an @IF nested in another goes with it. A tag after the @IF still counts.

Only the bare tag counts: @READONLY-SURVEY is read-only on the survey and writable on the form, so it is not one of these fields; nor is @READONLY-FORM, read-only on the form and writable on the survey. A field some page can write is not a field only the round writes.
